question_records.stem: Calculate the amount of substance in moles for 5.41 x 10^22 formula units of calcium nitrate, Ca(NO3)2(s).
Calculate the mass of 1.20 mol of potassium phosphate, K3PO4(s).
How many oxygen atoms are present in 2.25 mol of sulfur dioxide, SO2(g)?
A compound is 48.6% carbon, 8.16% hydrogen, and 43.2% oxygen by mass. Its molar mass is 74.1 g/mol. Determine the molecular formula of the compound.
question_records.answer_hint: Empirical formula C3H6O2; molecular formula C3H6O2

question_records.stem: In excess oxygen, phosphorus reacts to form tetraphosphorus decoxide, P4O10(s). Calculate the mass of P4O10 produced when 6.20 g of P4(s) is used.
question_records.answer_hint: 14.2 g P4O10 approximately after using P4 + 5O2 -> P4O10

question_records.stem: Sulfuric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide to produce sodium sulfate and water. If 4.90 g of H2SO4(aq) reacts completely with excess NaOH(aq), what mass of Na2SO4(s) is produced? Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction.

Use the lab data below to determine the percentage yield of lead(II) iodide, PbI2(s), produced when excess potassium iodide is added to lead(II) nitrate solution. Lab data: mass of Pb(NO3)2 used = 1.36 g; mass of clean, dry filter paper = 1.08 g; mass of dry precipitate and filter paper = 2.50 g. Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction.
question_records.answer_hint: Pb(NO3)2 + 2KI -> PbI2 + 2KNO3; actual precipitate mass = 1.42 g; theoretical yield is about 1.89 g PbI2; percentage yield is about 75.1%
